title: Independent Set by width of a supplied rank decomposition
task: Does G have at least k pairwise nonadjacent vertices?
encoding: A finite, simple, undirected, unweighted graph G and a nonnegative integer k.
parameter: The actual width of the supplied rank decomposition, denoted by p. Cut rank is computed over the binary field.
coverage: Historical ETH and independently reviewed recoveries.

reader.label: Subexponential bound in squared width
reader.title: Subexponential bound in squared width under ETH
reader.explanation: The source constructs a vertex order. The false-twin expansion preserves low supplied width, and a rank decomposition can be supplied by using the order along a caterpillar.

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm decides Independent Set within the stated running time.
qualifications: The exponent is a computable nonnegative integer function and has computable convergence to little-o at scale p^2.

reader.explanation: The proof uses paths to replace selection cliques and a triangle-free padding graph to force optimal certificates.

recoveryAssessments.comparison: The recovered clock is the same squared-width scale with a computable exponent and modulus. The restricted instances are valid inputs of the historical task and the normalized full graph encoding, including any supplied certificate, is polynomial in its order.

For every fixed positive exponent saving below two, the recovery excludes the corresponding power of the same width. The restricted instances are valid inputs of the historical task and the normalized full graph encoding, including any supplied certificate, is polynomial in its order.
